content.needs:
Project proposal

Keyit General Secondary School integrated smart management system and digital infrastructure
Mr. Shewayiraf

1. Introduction and strategic vision

Keyit General Secondary School is a government school. This project is not a simple website. It is meant to make the school a technology center of excellence at city-administration level and at regional level.

Part 1: Digital identity and the need for an .edu.et domain

The system was built by in-house staff. Linked with an official web address, it provides these benefits. An official web address is essential for the school's identity and security.

- Institutional trust: an .edu.et domain shows parents and international institutions that the school belongs to the government education system.
- Digital ownership: the school can have its own official email addresses (for example info@school.edu.et) and keep control of its information.
- Payment record: registration is done through Ethio Telecom. The yearly fee is paid by Telebirr or a legal bank receipt so the audit trail is clear.
- It makes it easier to work with charitable organizations that want to support the school.
- Staff and teachers can do their work from anywhere, meet students, and exchange files.
- Because the school has its own file system, students, teachers, and staff can use and share their files without being limited by distance.
- Smart classroom management: teachers can teach with digital content in class, and students can take part through their creative work.
- Student portal: a place where students and parents follow results, conduct, and homework.
- Innovation showcase: skilled students can present projects to regional and ministry officials through the website and raise the school's name.

Part 2: Hardware and infrastructure needs

1. Server room (central server unit)
- HP ProDesk/EliteDesk 800 G6 Core i7, 16GB RAM, 1TB HDD: a high-capacity computer chosen to run the management system and the student database.

2. Network installation
- 300 meters of Cat6 Ethernet cable, for fast data and a reliable link between rooms.
- 200 RJ45 connectors, for durable connections.
- Network switch rack (9U cabinet), so routers and switches stay in one place, protected from dust and unwanted contact.

3. Power supply and protection
- 10 or more heavy-duty extensions (APC/Huntkey) for each smart classroom, able to handle power fluctuation.

Part 3: Project budget

1. Main server computer — HP EliteDesk 800 G6 Tower (Intel Core i7, 16GB RAM, 1TB HDD/SSD, 24" monitor) — 1 — 85,000 ETB — total 85,000
2. Network cable — Cat6 Ethernet (high-speed copper, 305m roll, D-Link/Cisco) — 1 roll — 12,000 ETB — total 12,000
3. Power extension — APC SurgeArrest or Huntkey SZM (heavy duty, 5+ sockets, surge protection) — 10 — 2,500 ETB — total 25,000
4. Network connectors — RJ45 shielded, Cat6 compatible — 200 — 30 ETB — total 6,000
5. Server rack — 9U wall-mount cabinet with cooling fan and power strip — 1 — 18,000 ETB — total 18,000
6. Domain registration — .edu.et official Ethio Telecom registration, yearly — 1 year — 1,200 ETB — total 1,200
7. Installation labor — cable laying, server configuration, and network work — 1 lot — 15,000 ETB — total 15,000

Grand total: 162,200 ETB

1. Prices can change with the market, so at least three proforma invoices must be collected before purchase.
2. Power extensions and the network cable must be heavy duty, to protect the life of the server and the computers.
3. The .edu.et fee is renewed every year and must be told to the finance office in advance.

Part 4: Information security and privacy policy

The school's digital system is responsible for protecting users' information. This policy states how the school collects, stores, and protects that information.

1. Data collected
- Students: full name, age, sex, academic results, and conduct.
- Parents: name, phone number, and address (for emergencies and reports).
- Staff: employment status, education, and salary information.

2. How data is used
- To follow teaching and learning and to produce results.
- To prepare statistical reports required by the Ministry of Education and regional offices.
- To keep a clear link between the school and parents.
- No information is passed to a third party for advertising or any other purpose.

3. Security measures
- Each user enters the system only with a private password.
- Role-based access: teachers see only their own students' results. Only authorized finance staff can see financial records.
- Sensitive information stored on the server is protected by encryption.
- A daily backup is taken so information is not lost.

4. User rights
- Parents and students may ask for a correction when recorded information is wrong.
- When a student leaves, required records are kept as the law says, and the rest may be requested for deletion.

5. Policy updates
- The school may update this policy as technology and government rules change. Updates are posted on the website.

Confirmation: this policy is approved by Keyit General Secondary School management and is in force.
